input.prompt:
Topic: CSCI-488: CS Undergraduate Summer Co-op. This catalog entry has student-, instructor-, or term-specific content. Create a rigorous orientation companion that teaches the stable process, standards, planning methods, evaluation criteria, and representative examples without inventing a fixed RIT syllabus. Official catalog description: Students perform professional work related to Computer Science. Students must complete a student co-op work report for each term for which they are registered; students are also evaluated each term by their supervisor. A satisfactory grade is given for co-op when both a completed student co-op work report and a completed, corresponding supervisor evaluation are received and when both documents are generally consistent. When registered for co-op, students are considered by RIT to have full-time status. In order to register for co-op for summer term, we expect that students will work a minimum of 12 weeks and work a minimum of 35 hours per week. Prerequisite: CSCI-099 or equivalent course. Typically Offered: Summer

Source excerpts:

[acm-code-of-ethics]
The ACM Code directs computing professionals to contribute to society and human well-being. Computing professionals should avoid harm. They should be honest and trustworthy. They should be fair and take action not to discriminate. They should respect the work required to produce new ideas and creative works. They should respect privacy. They should honor confidentiality. Professionals should strive to achieve high quality in both processes and products. They should maintain high standards of professional competence, conduct, and ethical practice. Robust security should be designed and implemented when appropriate. Ethical computing decisions identify stakeholders, foreseeable benefits and harms, uncertainty, alternatives, and obligations.

[acm-research-practice]
Responsible technical communication distinguishes claims from evidence. It cites prior work and identifies the contribution being reported. Methods should be described well enough for readers to evaluate the work. Results should be reported accurately rather than selected to create a misleading conclusion. Limitations and threats to validity should be made visible. Authors should preserve research integrity and avoid plagiarism, fabrication, and falsification. Conflicts and relevant relationships should be disclosed according to publication policy. A research project narrows a question, reviews literature, defines a reproducible method, evaluates results, and communicates for the intended audience.

[rit-csci-488]
Students perform professional work related to Computer Science. Students must complete a student co-op work report for each term for which they are registered; students are also evaluated each term by their supervisor. A satisfactory grade is given for co-op when both a completed student co-op work report and a completed, corresponding supervisor evaluation are received and when both documents are generally consistent. When registered for co-op, students are considered by RIT to have full-time status. In order to register for co-op for summer term, we expect that students will work a minimum of 12 weeks and work a minimum of 35 hours per week. Prerequisite: CSCI-099 or equivalent course. Typically Offered: Summer

beats.example: A student submits a structured PDF report detailing project scope, technical challenges, and deliverables after the summer term.

beats.visualDirection: Render a document template with sections for 'Project Description', 'Technical Implementation', and 'Deliverables' to illustrate the report structure.

beats.claim: Students are evaluated each term by their assigned supervisor through a formal evaluation document.
beats.example: A supervisor completes a standardized form rating the student's technical contributions, communication, and professional conduct.
beats.title: Supervisor Evaluation Process
beats.visualDirection: Display a supervisor evaluation form layout with fields for 'Technical Competence', 'Professional Conduct', and 'Overall Assessment'.

beats.claim: A satisfactory grade is awarded only when both the student report and supervisor evaluation are generally consistent.
beats.example: The academic advisor reviews both documents and confirms that the student's self-assessment aligns with the supervisor's ratings before finalizing the grade.
beats.title: Grading Consistency Standard
beats.visualDirection: Create a two-column comparison table showing 'Student Report' and 'Supervisor Evaluation' with a central 'Consistency Check' column indicating alignment.

beats.claim: Computing professionals must avoid harm, be honest, and strive for high quality in both processes and products.
beats.example: A co-op student implements robust security measures and documents all code changes to ensure transparency and prevent unintended system harm.
beats.title: ACM Ethical Practice in Co-op
beats.visualDirection: Show a checklist graphic with icons representing 'Avoid Harm', 'Honesty', 'High Quality', and 'Robust Security' as co-op competencies.

beats.claim: Responsible technical communication requires distinguishing claims from evidence and citing prior work accurately.
beats.example: A student's co-op report includes a literature review section that explicitly cites prior research and clearly separates empirical results from theoretical claims.
beats.title: Responsible Technical Communication
beats.visualDirection: Display a before-and-after comparison of a paragraph showing how to properly distinguish 'claims' from 'evidence' using citation markers.

beats.claim: Authors should preserve research integrity by avoiding fabrication and ensuring methods are reproducible.
beats.example: A student maintains version-controlled code repositories and detailed methodology notes so that their co-op project can be independently verified.
beats.title: Research Integrity and Documentation
beats.visualDirection: Illustrate a workflow diagram showing 'Method Documentation', 'Version Control', and 'Reproducibility Check' as mandatory co-op practices.

beats.claim: Students must verify registration eligibility, document consistency, and ethical compliance before term completion.
beats.example: A student uses a final checklist to confirm 12-week/35-hour commitment, report-supervisor alignment, and ACM ethical standards before submitting grades.
beats.title: Practical Analysis Checklist
beats.visualDirection: Provide a compact checklist graphic with three main categories: 'Registration & Hours', 'Documentation Consistency', and 'Ethical & Research Standards', each with a checkbox.

learningObjectives: Students will define the minimum time and credit requirements for summer co-op registration.
Students will articulate the dual-document grading mechanism and consistency standard for co-op evaluation.
Students will apply ACM ethical principles and responsible research practices to professional co-op work.
